THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Spicy Fajita Chicken Gnocchi

This replaces ordering takeout on weeknights. Crispy gnocchi, creamy spicy sauce, and a kid plate that's ready in the same 30 minutes — no separate meal, no compromise.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME30 min
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING425 cal | 35g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: Don't sauce everything before splitting — sauce goes in AFTER the split point.

Ingredients

BASE

  • 1 pack shelf-stable gnocchi (~16 oz)
  • 2-2.5 cups cooked shredded chicken

SHARED SAUCE BASE (NEUTRAL)

  • 3/4 cup cottage cheese
  • 1/2 cup Fairlife fat-free milk

FINISH

  • Juice of 1 lime
  • Optional: green onions

Option A — Mild Creamy

  • Small amount of blended sauce base (no chili oil, no spice)
  • Shredded mild cheese (mozz or cheddar)

Option C — Dry Plate (lowest friction)

  • Optional: ketchup or mild dipping sauce on side

VEG

  • 1 bell pepper, sliced
  • 1/2 onion, sliced

ADULT ADD-ONS

  • 1-1.5 tsp Dan-O's (Outlaw preferred)
  • 1 tsp smoked paprika
  • 1 tsp garlic powder
  • 1 tsp onion powder
  • 1 tsp chili oil
  • Optional: chili flakes

Option B — Rao's Alfredo

  • 2-3 tbsp Rao's Alfredo sauce
  • Optional: shredded mild cheese on top

Allergens: dairy, gluten.

STOP. Chicken is crisped. Divide gnocchi, chicken, and veg into 2 pans NOW — everything after this point is different for adults and kids.

Method

Shared base

  1. 1.CRISP THE GNOCCHI. Medium-high heat, 2 tsp oil. Add gnocchi in a single layer. Cook 8-10 min, flipping occasionally. Goal: crispy outside, not soft. Set aside.
  2. 2.COOK VEG. Same pan, high heat. Add peppers + onions. Cook 4-5 min until lightly charred. Set aside.
  3. 3.CRISP CHICKEN. Add shredded chicken to pan. Let it sit — develop slight browning. Don't stir constantly.

Adult — Spicy Fajita

  1. 4.BUILD FLAVOR SAUCE. Blend cottage cheese + milk until smooth. Add to adult pan. Mix in Dan-O's, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, chili oil. Simmer 2-3 min. Should look like a light creamy sauce, not thick paste.
  2. 5.COMBINE. Add gnocchi + veggies to adult pan. Toss lightly — should coat, not drown.
  3. 6.FINISH. Lime squeeze + optional green onions. This completes the dish — don't skip.

Kid Path — Simple + Fast · Option A — Mild Creamy

  1. 4.MILD SAUCE. Add a small amount of the blended cottage cheese + milk to kid pan (NO spices, NO chili oil). Stir with chicken.
  2. 5.COMBINE. Add gnocchi. Add shredded cheese on top. Toss gently — keep it creamy and familiar.

Kid Path — Simple + Fast · Option B — Rao's Alfredo

  1. 4.SAUCE. Warm 2-3 tbsp Rao's Alfredo in the kid pan. Skip the cottage cheese sauce entirely for this option.
  2. 5.COMBINE. Add gnocchi + chicken (or kid protein swap). Toss in Rao's until coated. Add cheese if they want it.

Kid Path — Simple + Fast · Option C — Dry Plate (lowest friction)

  1. 4.PLATE. Gnocchi + chicken only. No sauce. Veg on side — not mixed in.
  2. 5.SERVE. Optional ketchup or mild sauce on the side for dipping.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult — Spicy Fajita: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid Path — Simple + Fast: Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • Don't overcook after sauce — breaks texture. Simmer 2-3 min max.
  • Don't force veggies into kid portion — serve on side, they eat more when they choose.

If something fails

Gnocchi is soggy / soft: You either boiled it or crowded the pan. Single layer, medium-high heat, don't touch for 3-4 min per side. If using frozen gnocchi, thaw first.

Sauce is grainy / chunky: Blend longer — full 60 seconds on high. Cottage cheese must be completely smooth before it hits the pan.

Sauce is too thick / paste-like: Add more milk, 1 tbsp at a time. You want it to coat a spoon, not clump.

Dish tastes flat: You skipped the lime. Squeeze half a lime over the finished dish — acid is what ties everything together.

Too heavy / rich: You used too much sauce. The sauce should coat the gnocchi, not pool at the bottom of the pan. Less is more.

Storage and reheating

Store: Store gnocchi + sauce together (the crisp won't survive anyway). Keep chicken separate if possible.

Reheat: Microwave 90 sec or pan reheat with a splash of milk to loosen the sauce. The gnocchi won't re-crisp — that's the tradeoff. Fresh is best for this one.

Lasts: 2-3 days in fridge. Best eaten same day for texture.

Brands I use

Fairlife
Fat-free milk
Higher protein per serving than regular milk, lactose-free
Dan-O's
Outlaw seasoning
All-purpose spice blend with heat — replaces 4-5 individual spices
Del Real
Shredded chicken
Pre-cooked, saves 20+ min, consistent shred texture
Rao's
Alfredo sauce
Kid Option B — store-bought shortcut that actually tastes good. Skip the cottage cheese sauce for kids who want familiar flavor.
